ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog has a brownish-grey body with a dark mid-dorsal pattern. It features a pointed snout, a narrow mouth, and distinct dark lateral bands extending from the eyes to the groin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla mymensinghensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, V-shaped or chevron-like marking on its back, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Microhyla mymensinghensis* inhabits moist, low-lying areas in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in grassy wetlands, paddy fields, and floodplains at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Mymensingh Narrow-mouthed Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging from soil or leaf litter after dark to forage for small invertebrates like ants and termites.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla mymensinghensis* breeds in temporary rain pools during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs that hatch into free-swimming larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microhyla mymensinghensis* is found in the plains of Bangladesh and adjacent parts of Northeast India, typically inhabiting low-elevation wetlands and agricultural areas.
ai.callDescription: The Mymensingh Narrow-mouthed Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like buzzing trill that is heard emanating from shallow, temporary rain pools and flooded agricultural fields.
